criteria.name: Mission concept and rationale — What will it do, who are the users, why is it needed?
criteria.reasoning: Clear mission purpose (GBR bleaching monitoring), explicit users (marine/conservation scientists), strong rationale with cited literature on bleaching, reef size, and Asner's imaging technique. Requirements not yet formalised, but concept and need are well established.

evidence.quote: A near-real-time relay to monitoring stations on the ground would allow marine and conservation scientists to more accurately predict and react to coral bleaching events.
Reef-monitoring satellites could also be used to report sea surface temperatures, thermal stress on coral, and bathymetry

criteria.name: Project plan — How you plan to complete the assignment, including either a Gantt chart or a timetable and information sources you plan to use
criteria.reasoning: Detailed Gantt chart with weekly tasks, colour-coded status, deadlines, and task-by-task narrative tied to mission needs (launch, orbit, ground control, comms). However, no explicit contingency/variation provision, which the Accomplished descriptor requires; hence lower end of band.

evidence.quote: Project work will be divided into weeks via a Gantt Chart. Detailed task descriptions can be found on the next page.
Week 10 is reserved for review, amendments, final simulations, and reflection.

criteria.name: Preliminary progress — Technical content and evidence of sufficient work done to date
criteria.reasoning: Evidence of progress is background research and STK tutorials only; no preliminary technical results, calculations, orbit or payload figures are presented or interpreted. On track, but technical output is minor.

evidence.quote: I have read the brief of Asner’s monitoring system in Hawaii, researched into how coral bleaching occurs and its severity

criteria.name: Report presentation
criteria.reasoning: Well-written, clear structure with headings, good Gantt figure. But references are bare URLs as footnotes with no formal reference list, and in-text citation style is inconsistent; 'Useful Links' section is informal. Falls short of professional referencing standard.

evidence.quote: Completed stages are gold. Incomplete stages are blue. Deadlines are indicated by red lines.

technical_issues.issue: Claims near-real-time relay without discussing orbit/coverage implications (e.g. LEO revisit gaps vs GEO); feasibility not yet addressed.
No contingency planning for schedule slippage; 'End of Life' options listed without technical screening.

overall: Strong, well-referenced mission concept for GBR monitoring with a detailed Gantt plan and STK chosen. Preliminary technical work is thin (tutorials only), and referencing/presentation is informal rather than professional. Solid Part 1 submission.

feedback.summary: A strong Part 1 submission. Your mission concept for Great Barrier Reef bleaching monitoring is clear, well-justified and well-referenced, and your Gantt chart shows a detailed weekly plan. To reach the top band, formalise mission requirements, add contingency planning, present preliminary STK results, and adopt a professional referencing style.
next_steps: Add a formal requirements section (goals, objectives, requirements) linking each requirement to user needs, and address orbit/coverage feasibility for your near-real-time relay claim (e.g. LEO revisit gaps vs GEO).
Add contingency/variation provisions to your project plan (e.g. buffer weeks, fallback tasks if STK simulations slip) and briefly justify End-of-Life options with technical screening.
Include preliminary technical results from STK (orbit plots, coverage/revisit figures) with brief interpretation, and replace footnote URLs with a formal reference list cited consistently in text.

criteria.C1: Your Mission Concept & Rationale clearly states the purpose (GBR bleaching monitoring), identifies users (marine and conservation scientists), and supports the rationale with cited literature on bleaching, reef scale and Asner's imaging technique — well into the Accomplished band. To consolidate this level, formalise mission goals, objectives and requirements, and discuss the orbit/coverage implications of your near-real-time relay claim.
criteria.C2: Your Gantt chart with weekly tasks, colour-coded status, deadlines and task-by-task narrative tied to mission needs is detailed and credible. The Accomplished descriptor also requires provision for variations and contingencies, which is currently missing — adding schedule-slippage contingencies and technical screening of End-of-Life options would secure the top of the band.
criteria.C3: Your progress evidence is background research and STK tutorials 1–4, which sits in the Adequate band. The Accomplished level requires a preliminary set of results with brief description or interpretation — include early STK outputs (e.g. orbit or coverage figures) and interpret them to show technical progress.
criteria.C4: Your report is well-written with clear headings and a good Gantt figure, but referencing is informal: bare URLs as footnotes, no formal reference list, inconsistent in-text citation, and an informal 'Useful Links' section. Adopting a consistent citation style with a matching reference list would lift presentation to the Accomplished level.
